# 2020 Global Opportunities Report

Report 020 | Published 2020-05-20 | Evaluated 2026-11-07

[Original member article](https://www.lynalden.com/2020-5-20/) | [Article index](README.md) | [Structured review](../data/reviews/020.json)

Country valuation, currency and external-balance screening.

This article is a summary of a separate country-ranking report, so the complete ranked strategy is not auditable from this page alone. The currency-denomination distinction is useful, but the necessary-current-account-surplus claim is demonstrably wrong because NIIP includes valuation and exchange-rate changes.

**Coverage:** All numbered text blocks and image labels read. Material theses, forecasts and explanations are included; routine holdings lists, incidental statistics, company descriptions and boilerplate are excluded. Chart pixels were not inspected.

### 020-C05

**Foreign-currency debt increases vulnerability**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Right |
| Type | explanation |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | Emerging markets |
| Source blocks | 15, 18, 19 |
| Thesis family | dollar-em-debt |

The Fed funding review substantiates the wider dollar-financing stress channel. A sovereign reserve total is not automatically available to every private borrower; currency denomination, maturity, hedges and export receipts must be assessed together.

**Direction:** Resolved as stated.

**Timing:** No fixed endpoint supplied.

**Mechanism:** Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Outcome evidence:**

- [Financial Stability Report: funding risk](https://www.federalreserve.gov/publications/may-2021-funding-risk.htm) | Federal Reserve | 2021-05-06 | Verified in the audit

March 2020 global dollar funding pressures increased as wholesale funding contracted and hedging/credit-line demand rose. Swap-funded auctions helped foreign banks meet commitments and build liquid assets without selling dollar assets.

The sharp 2020 oil-price decline supplies a relevant external-income shock. To attribute currency depreciation requires actual exchange-rate, production, fiscal and portfolio-flow data; reserves are a buffer, not a fixed exchange-rate guarantee.

**Direction:** See reason; no return inferred.

**Timing:** No fixed endpoint supplied.

**Mechanism:** Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Outcome evidence:**

- [Brent spot crude price](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DCOILBRENTEU) | EIA via FRED | Verified in the audit

Daily USD/barrel observations: 69.08 on January 3, 2020; 9.12 on April 21, 2020; 78.61 on December 30, 2021; 82.82 on December 30, 2022. These are spot prices, not futures-investment returns.

### 020-C10

**NIIP distinguishes creditors from debtors**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Mixed |
| Type | explanation |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | External balance sheets |
| Source blocks | 31, 32, 33 |
| Thesis family | niip-stock-flow |

Assets minus liabilities is the correct stock identity. Equity liabilities are not debt promises, and valuation changes can dominate annual movements, so debtor language should not imply all net liabilities require fixed repayment.

**Direction:** See reason; no return inferred.

**Timing:** No fixed endpoint supplied.

**Mechanism:** Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Outcome evidence:**

- [2022 international investment position](https://www.bea.gov/news/2023/us-international-investment-position-4th-quarter-and-year-2022) | BEA | 2023-03-29 | Verified in the audit

US NIIP improved $2.01 trillion in 2022 despite negative net financial transactions of $677.1 b. Other valuation changes added $2.68 trillion; US asset-price declines lowered external liabilities more than assets. A current-account surplus is not required for an NIIP improvement.

### 020-C11

**Current-account surplus is required for improvement**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Wrong |
| Type | explanation |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | US NIIP |
| Source blocks | 34 |
| Thesis family | niip-current-account-necessity |

BEA reported NIIP improved $2.01 trillion in 2022 while the US ran a $943.8 b current-account deficit. Relative asset-price changes added enough valuation gains to overwhelm negative financial flows. A surplus helps cumulatively, but is not a necessary condition for reversing the ratio or stock deterioration.

**Direction:** See reason; no return inferred.

**Timing:** No fixed endpoint supplied.

**Mechanism:** Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** high

**Outcome evidence:**

- [2022 international investment position](https://www.bea.gov/news/2023/us-international-investment-position-4th-quarter-and-year-2022) | BEA | 2023-03-29 | Verified in the audit

US NIIP improved $2.01 trillion in 2022 despite negative net financial transactions of $677.1 b. Other valuation changes added $2.68 trillion; US asset-price declines lowered external liabilities more than assets. A current-account surplus is not required for an NIIP improvement.

- [2022 international transactions](https://www.bea.gov/index.php/news/2023/us-international-transactions-4th-quarter-and-year-2022) | BEA | 2023-03-23 | Verified in the audit

The 2022 US current-account deficit was initially reported $943.8 b, 3.7% GDP. This coincided with an improving 2022 NIIP in the separately published position statistics.

### 020-C12

**Weaker dollar can improve US position**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Mixed |
| Type | explanation |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | US external assets |
| Source blocks | 34 |
| Thesis family | niip-currency-valuation |

Foreign-currency asset values rise in dollar terms when the dollar weakens, other things equal. In 2022 NIIP improved despite a stronger dollar because relative asset-price effects dominated, illustrating why the FX channel is only one component.

**Direction:** See reason; no return inferred.

**Timing:** No fixed endpoint supplied.

**Mechanism:** Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium
